Differentiation timing score Differentiation timing score PCA-based scoring of differentiation timing from bulk RNA-seq time-course data Author: Zoheb Khan Created: 2025-08-29 Modified: 2026-08-01 Compiled: 2026-08-01 Environment: R 4.6.1; Bioconductor 3.23 Dependencies: AnnotationDbi 1.74.0; bookdown 0.47; circlize 0.4.18; clusterProfiler 4.20.0; ComplexHeatmap 2.28.0; DESeq2 1.52.0; edgeR 4.10.1; ggplot2 4.0.3; ggrepel 0.9.8; knitr 1.51; org.Hs.eg.db 3.23.1; patchwork 1.3.2; ragg 1.5.2; scales 1.4.0; svglite 2.2.2; systemfonts 1.3.2; viridis 0.6.5; yaml 2.3.12 Source: github.com/ZohebKhan1/pca-maturation-scoring 1 Introduction This tutorial develops a reference-trajectory score for bulk RNA-seq differentiation time courses. The worked example uses 192 processed GSE122380 samples spanning days 1 through 15 and 13 independent induced pluripotent stem cell lines. A reference time course defines the expression space and trajectory; each sample is then assigned a continuous position along that trajectory. The workflow has four operations: select temporal genes from the reference samples; train a centered, unscaled PCA model on those genes; join ordered day centroids into a piecewise-linear trajectory; and project samples to their nearest position on that finite trajectory. The maintained analysis is in scripts/01_build_tutorial_objects.R. The reusable scorer is functions/score_differentiation_timing.R. The tutorial source lives only in tutorial/; docs/ is the generated GitHub Pages site. 1.1 Reuse the scorer The scorer assumes that temporal genes and normalized expression values have already been defined. It trains the reference PCA and day-centroid polyline, projects all supplied samples into that fixed space, and returns predicted time, a normalized differentiation score, and projection-distance diagnostics. It does not select genes, normalize counts, draw figures, or write files. base_url <- paste0( 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZohebKhan1/', 'pca-maturation-scoring/main/functions' ) download.file( paste0(base_url, '/score_differentiation_timing.R'), 'score_differentiation_timing.R' ) source('score_differentiation_timing.R') The primary inputs are: expression_matrix: normalized expression, with unique gene IDs in rows and unique sample IDs in columns; metadata: one row per expression sample; temporal_genes: gene IDs selected independently of the samples being evaluated; sample_id_col and time_col: metadata columns containing sample IDs and numeric reference times; reference_col and reference_values: optional metadata fields that distinguish training samples from samples to score; and n_pcs: the retained PCA dimensions used for projection, set to three here. The output list contains scores, pca_coordinates, pca_fit, centroid_polyline, retained temporal_genes, and the reference_time_range. Because projection is clipped to finite centroid-to-centroid segments, predicted times and normalized scores are bounded by the first and last reference timepoints. A score outside 0 to 1 is therefore not part of this implementation’s contract. 2 Data and scope The example uses GSE122380, an iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte differentiation bulk RNA-seq time course reported by Strober, Elorbany, Rhodes and colleagues. The repository tracks aligned sample metadata, a raw-count matrix, and a variance-stabilized expression matrix. The active input contains no perturbation samples; all 192 samples define the full reference trajectory. The tracked RDS files are the reproducible starting point for this repository. The raw-read acquisition, QC, alignment, quantification, filtering, and construction of the tracked VST matrix are not included, so this tutorial does not claim end-to-end reproducibility from FASTQ files. Pearson correlation between day-mean profiles from the same variable-gene set. 3 Scoring workflow 3.1 Select temporal genes Genes must pass three sequential filters. First, a gene’s maximum day-mean TMM-normalized CPM must be at least 10. Second, a DESeq2 likelihood-ratio test (LRT) must have a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value below \(10^{-7}\). Third, the range of day-mean VST expression must be at least 0.6. The LRT compares a full count model containing cell line and categorical differentiation day with a reduced model containing cell line alone: \[ \mathrm{full}: y \sim \mathrm{cell\ line} + \mathrm{day}, \qquad \mathrm{reduced}: y \sim \mathrm{cell\ line}. \tag{1} \] The likelihood-ratio statistic is \[ \mathrm{LR} = 2\left(\ell_{\mathrm{full}} - \ell_{\mathrm{reduced}}\right), \tag{2} \] where \(\ell\) is the maximized model log likelihood. This tests whether categorical day improves fit after accounting for cell-line structure; it does not assume a linear expression trend. source('functions/select_temporal_genes.R') analysis_params <- yaml::read_yaml('config/analysis.yml') temporal_gene_params <- analysis_params$temporal_gene_selection temporal_selection <- select_temporal_genes( counts = counts, vst = vst, metadata = metadata, expression_cpm_cutoff = temporal_gene_params$expression_cpm_cutoff, lrt_padj_cutoff = temporal_gene_params$lrt_padj_cutoff, vst_dynamic_range_cutoff = temporal_gene_params$vst_dynamic_range_cutoff ) temporal_genes <- temporal_selection$temporal_genes Table 3.1: Sequential temporal-gene filtering. PCA is trained after centering each gene without variance scaling. If \(\mathbf{x}_i\) is sample \(i\), \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) is the reference gene-mean vector, and \(W_k\) contains the retained loading vectors, then \[ \mathbf{z}_i = (\mathbf{x}_i - \boldsymbol{\mu}) W_k. \tag{3} \] The scorer retains three PCs. PC1 is flipped for figure readability when needed so it increases with differentiation day; a sign flip does not alter Euclidean projections or scores. Figure 4. PCA and PC1-day relationships for the full temporal set and two descriptive cluster subsets. C1+C2 and C3+C4 are interpretive subsets, not alternative primary models. The loading analysis annotates the largest PC1 and PC2 loadings and tests the top 500 genes in each PC1 direction for GO enrichment against the full temporal-gene universe. Figure 5. PCA loading interpretation. a-b. The ten largest positive and negative PC1 and PC2 loading genes. Ambiguous Ensembl-to-symbol mappings retain the Ensembl ID. c-d. GO enrichment among the 500 strongest negative and positive PC1 loadings. 3.3 Fit and score the day-centroid polyline For each ordered reference day \(t_j\), the mean PCA coordinate is \[ \mathbf{c}_j = \frac{1}{|I_j|}\sum_{i \in I_j}\mathbf{z}_i, \qquad j = 1,\ldots,m. \tag{4} \] The ordered centroids define a piecewise-linear trajectory. Segment \(j\) begins at \(\mathbf{a}_j=\mathbf{c}_j\), ends at \(\mathbf{b}_j=\mathbf{c}_{j+1}\), and has direction \(\mathbf{v}_j=\mathbf{b}_j-\mathbf{a}_j\). For sample \(i\), the fraction along segment \(j\) is \[ \alpha_{ij} = \operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]} \left( \frac{\langle \mathbf{z}_i-\mathbf{a}_j,\mathbf{v}_j \rangle} {\langle \mathbf{v}_j,\mathbf{v}_j \rangle} \right). \tag{5} \] The closest finite-segment projection is selected: \[ \mathbf{q}_{ij}=\mathbf{a}_j+\alpha_{ij}\mathbf{v}_j, \qquad j^\ast=\underset{j}{\operatorname{argmin}} \left\lVert\mathbf{z}_i-\mathbf{q}_{ij}\right\rVert^2. \tag{6} \] The corresponding predicted time and normalized score are \[ \widehat{t}_i=t_{j^\ast}+\alpha_{ij^\ast}(t_{j^\ast+1}-t_{j^\ast}), \qquad s_i=\frac{\widehat{t}_i-t_{\mathrm{start}}}{t_{\mathrm{end}}-t_{\mathrm{start}}}. \tag{7} \] Zero-length centroid segments are omitted. The method assumes that ordered centroids describe a meaningful trajectory in retained PC space. A self-approaching or folded trajectory can make nearest-segment assignments biologically ambiguous; squared projection distance should therefore be inspected when adapting the scorer. source('functions/score_differentiation_timing.R') timing_fit <- score_differentiation_timing( expression_matrix = vst, metadata = metadata, temporal_genes = temporal_genes, sample_id_col = 'sample_id', time_col = 'day_numeric', n_pcs = analysis_params$timing_score$n_pcs ) head(timing_fit$scores) Figure 6. Dashed lines mark the bounded reference endpoints at 0 and 1. 4 Internal cell-line cross-validation Leave-one-cell-line-out validation repeats temporal-gene selection, PCA training, and polyline fitting using the remaining cell lines, then scores samples from the held-out cell line. The count-based DESeq2 LRT is refit in each fold. The tracked VST matrix is shared across folds because the upstream transformation pipeline is not available; the result is therefore internal validation conditional on this processed cohort, not an external transferability estimate. Fold-specific temporal genes are also divided into maturation and progenitor sets by the sign of their Spearman correlation with day. The reported accuracy metrics use the complete temporal set. All 13 held-out cell lines contribute; cell line 19190 is omitted only from the per-cell-line panel grid so the display remains a balanced 3-by-4 layout. It does not establish cell quality, differentiation efficiency, lineage identity, potency, or biological directionality. For a new study, select temporal genes and train the PCA/polyline model in an appropriate reference cohort, then project test samples without refitting that model. Before comparing scores across datasets, verify gene identifiers, normalization, shared feature support, batch structure, reference-time coverage, and projection distance. 6 References Love MI, Huber W, Anders S.
